PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS.expected_behavior: spec.prereg 11.2: two synthetic hosts with identical template structure and different slot values yield AGF > 0.8 against a shuffled null of about 0, confirming the extraction and comparison pipeline detects known cross-site structural correspondence.
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS.observed_behavior: AGF 0.5833333333333334 (14 matched instances / 24 signatures), mean pairwise Jaccard 1.0, 1 of 1 host pairs with nonzero shared structure. Observed AGF exceeds the powered NC-SIG-REASSIGN null p95 of 0.5; observed Jaccard 1.0 exceeds that null's Jaccard p95 of 0.8181818181818182. The prescribed label-permutation null is exactly degenerate (1 distinct value over 1000 permutations, std 0.0).
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS.pass_basis: Pipeline sensitivity is CONFIRMED by two powered comparisons (AGF vs NC-SIG-REASSIGN p95, and Jaccard == 1.0) and by 1/1 pairs sharing structure.
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS.frozen_threshold_caveat: The frozen expected value AGF > 0.8 is arithmetically unreachable on the frozen 2-host design under the frozen prereg 7.3 AGF definition: with n signatures per host and every key distinct and matched 1:1, matched instances = n and total signatures = 2n, so AGF = 0.5 exactly. Observed 0.583 exceeds that ceiling because 2 of the 14 matched instances come from duplicated keys. The threshold miss must not be read as a sensitivity failure.

PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION.expected_behavior: Not frozen. Added because the frozen 2-host control has one free label permutation, which is symmetric, so its prescribed null is exactly degenerate by the same identity that makes the main null degenerate. This 4-host extension supplies a permutation null with power; hosts C and D are deliberately unrelated to each other and to A/B.
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION.observed_behavior: AGF 0.4666666666666667, mean pairwise Jaccard 0.16666666666666666, 1 of 6 host pairs with nonzero shared structure (the A/B pair, Jaccard 1.0) and 5 of 6 with exactly zero shared structure. Observed Jaccard 0.16667 exceeds the NC-SIG-REASSIGN Jaccard p95 of 0.1645546814296814 (518 distinct null values).
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION.pass_basis: Pipeline both detects known correspondence (1/1 related pair, Jaccard 1.0, above the powered null) and discriminates unrelated structure (5/5 unrelated pairs yield Jaccard exactly 0.0).
PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS-4SITE-POWER-EXTENSION.residual_limitation: The primary AGF is NOT separable at this control size: with 30 signatures over 4 hosts the NC-SIG-REASSIGN lattice is coarse enough to reach the observed 0.4666666666666667, so observed_agf_exceeds_null_p95 is false. That is underpower at 30 signatures, not a negative result.

NC-SHUFFLED-HOST.expected_behavior: spec.prereg 8.1/8.2: permute eTLD+1 labels 1,000 times, recompute AGF, and verify the null distribution has std > 0 and that null p95 is below the observed AGF point estimate.
NC-SHUFFLED-HOST.observed_behavior: 1000 permutations produced exactly 1 distinct AGF value, 83.51083467094703, identical bitwise to the observed point estimate. std = 0.0, p95 = point estimate. The frozen secondary metric is likewise invariant: mean pairwise Jaccard also took exactly 1 distinct value.
NC-SHUFFLED-HOST.failure_mode: non-discriminating by algebraic construction, not by weakness
NC-SHUFFLED-HOST.pass_reason: AGF = sum_K (T_K^2 - sum_s n_{s,K}^2) / (2 * total_signatures) depends on the per-host signature counts of each key only through the symmetric quantity sum_s n_{s,K}^2. Permuting the eTLD+1 labels is a bijection on hosts, so it permutes the vector (n_{s,K})_s and leaves every sum_s n_{s,K}^2, hence every T_K, hence AGF, exactly invariant. The frozen control therefore detects nothing by construction. The same identity makes the frozen 2-host positive control null degenerate, which is why the powered extension above was necessary.
NC-SHUFFLED-HOST.consequence: The frozen primary clause AGF_point > null_p95 reduces to 83.51083467094703 > 83.51083467094703 and carries no information. metrics.decision_rule_evaluation.primary_evaluable is false and primary_satisfied is null, NOT false.

NC-SINGLETON-SITE.expected_behavior: spec.null_control: identify sites with no structural match to any other site in the sample, to verify zero-fraction handling.
NC-SINGLETON-SITE.observed_behavior: 0 of 15 hosts were singletons; every host shares at least one signature key with at least one other host. Zero-fraction handling was exercised and is correct (the PC-EXT control produced 5 of 6 pairs with exactly zero shared structure).
NC-SINGLETON-SITE.pass_reason: The zero-fraction code path is demonstrably exercised and produces exact zeros, so the absence of singletons in the real sample is a property of the sample rather than of the implementation.

observations: RAW: 177 anonymous HTTP(S) GETs were issued to 23 distinct hosts, 20 of which were the pre-registered base hosts. 155 pages were retained. No credential, registry authentication, browser binary or model API key was used at any point; the run required only outbound public HTTP.

RAW: 15 of the 20 pre-registered hosts yielded at least 2 pages, which satisfies the frozen validity sub-condition n_eTLD1_ge_2pages >= 10. The other 5 yielded exactly 1 page each and are recorded as NOT_MEASURED with their exact blocking artefact, not as a negative: npmjs.com, sourceforge.net and stackoverflow.com returned HTTP 403 on the homepage under the frozen User-Agent SPIDER-Research/1.0 (recorded in raw/raw_responses.jsonl); crates.io returned HTTP 200 but exposed zero same-origin anchor hrefs (client-rendered application); kernel.org returned HTTP 200 but exposed zero same-origin anchor hrefs (static page linking only to external mirrors). The robots.txt fetches independently corroborate that the two most important blocks are host-level edge behaviour rather than per-path site policy: www.npmjs.com/robots.txt returned HTTP 403 and stackoverflow.com/robots.txt returned HTTP 418, so the sample's three largest developer-package and developer-QA hubs are structurally unreachable to any probe presenting the frozen SPIDER-Research/1.0 identity.

RAW: 6 of the 20 pre-registered eTLD+1 labels are not registrable domains under the public suffix list. docs.python.org resolves to python.org, en.wikipedia.org to wikipedia.org, news.ycombinator.com to ycombinator.com, developer.mozilla.org to mozilla.org, dockerhub.io to docker.com and readthedocs.io to readthedocs.com. The frozen prereg host labels were used as the bootstrap and shuffle unit as specified; the derived registrable domains are recorded per site in raw/fetch_manifest.json.

RAW: 3 of the 20 frozen base URLs crossed to a different host on redirect: gitlab.com to about.gitlab.com, linuxfoundation.org to www.linuxfoundation.org, and readthedocs.io to about.readthedocs.com. The frozen sample entry for gitlab.com therefore measured a corporate marketing site rather than the developer platform, and the readthedocs.io entry measured a corporate site rather than a documentation host. Recorded in raw/fetch_manifest.json under notes and homepage_crossed_host.

RAW: en.wikipedia.org had 4 same-origin URLs disallowed by robots.txt (Special:Random, Special:RecentChanges, Special:SpecialPages, Special:Search) and was not crawled past its 10-page cap. gnu.org had 1 disallowed (/cgi-bin/estseek.cgi) and news.ycombinator.com had 1 (/vote). news.ycombinator.com additionally returned HTTP 429 on 2 further discovered URLs. gitlab.com had no robots-disallowed URLs.

validity_notes: The frozen design's primary scientific clause cannot return a verdict, and this must not be read as a result about C-CROSSSITE. The frozen NC-SHUFFLED-HOST permutation is an exact algebraic identity on the frozen AGF estimator, so the frozen decision rule reduces to 83.51083467094703 > 83.51083467094703. metrics.decision_rule_evaluation.primary_satisfied is null, not false, and primary_evaluable is false. The frozen validity sub-condition null_std > 0 fails for this reason.

This is a defect in the frozen estimator/null pair, not an environmental or infrastructure failure, and not a scientific negative. No substrate was missing, 0 pages failed extraction, and all 177 HTTP requests succeeded or failed in ways recorded per URL. The director_mandate portfolio_assessment names this exact failure class (an estimator that cannot see its own failure mode, and a keyed-group construction that silently resolves zero cells); no prerequisite was added in response to it.

The frozen positive control's numeric threshold is also unreachable by construction. spec.prereg 11.2 expects AGF > 0.8 on a 2-host design, but the frozen prereg 7.3 AGF definition caps a 2-host design at 0.5 when keys are distinct and matched 1:1. Observed 0.583 exceeds that ceiling. Pipeline sensitivity is nonetheless confirmed against two powered comparisons, so PC-SYNTHETIC-ALIAS passes on its stated purpose and its threshold must be treated as a design defect.

Representation loss 1 of 4: no JavaScript execution. The frozen prereg mandates HTTP-only extraction. This materially under-samples client-rendered sites and is the most likely reason crates.io yielded zero discoverable pages. Any site whose navigational or interaction structure is rendered client-side contributes no interaction structure at all to AGF. The measured AGF is therefore a lower bound on the HTTP-observable cross-site structure of this sample and says nothing about the JS-observable remainder.

Representation loss 2 of 4: B-A11Y-TREE is the preregistered approximation from semantic HTML, roles, aria-* and heading levels, not a browser accessibility tree, because no browser binary was available and the frozen prereg forbids requiring one. It is a lower bound on true accessibility-tree cost, so the measured 22.01x token ratio is an upper bound on the real advantage over an accessibility tree.

Representation loss 3 of 4: tokenizer convention. Tokens are cl100k_base (n_vocab 100277), the frozen convention. Token counts are a reporting convention, not a billing fact, and no model API was called, so no provider price is implied. The ratios between representations are tokenizer-robust because all four use the same encoder; the absolute token counts are not portable to other tokenizers.

Representation loss 4 of 4: the typed-slot parameterization rule is a heuristic. Any single-segment path templates to /{slug}, so structurally unlike sites can share a template. This inflates AGF for every population, including the nulls, and is why the host-coverage decomposition rather than the AGF magnitude is the informative result. 66.13% of signatures carry at least one typed slot.

Sampling validity: 15 of 20 pre-registered hosts are measured, all 15 reachable hosts contributing the full 10-page cap, so the sample is not thinned within the hosts that responded. The 5 unmeasured hosts are all developer/package-ecosystem platforms that block or client-render; their absence is not evidence about them. Because 4 of 5 failed for the same reason (edge blocking the frozen User-Agent), the surviving sample is biased toward documentation, reference and foundation sites, which are the least e-commerce-like members of the frozen sample.

Frozen-sample fidelity deviation: 3 of 20 base URLs redirected to a different host, so the gitlab.com, linuxfoundation.org and readthedocs.io entries measured corporate sites rather the sites named in prereg 5.2. Recorded in raw/fetch_manifest.json. This was not corrected, because the frozen sample is immutable and the prereg forbids adaptive sampling.

Snapshot timing: pages were fetched over 37 seconds (2026-09-27T02:32:12Z to 2026-09-27T02:32:49Z) with 5 concurrent workers, one sequential queue per host, at a 1.05 s per-host minimum interval. Each URL was fetched exactly once; the retained body is the only fetch of that URL. No site structure change during the window can be distinguished from between-site differences, and no re-fetch was used to detect it.

Polite-crawl compliance: robots.txt was fetched once per host before any page request and honoured wherever a parsable body was returned; static-asset and account/auth paths were excluded; and the per-host rate never exceeded 1 request per 1.05 s. Total load was 177 requests across 23 hosts for 155 retained pages. Two hosts returned non-robots bodies (stackoverflow.com HTTP 418, www.npmjs.com HTTP 403), so no rules were parsed or applied for them; because both of those hosts' homepages were also blocked, this did not cause any page to be fetched against stated rules, but the packet does not claim robots compliance was verified for those two hosts.

Estimator verification: the frozen AGF and mean pairwise Jaccard were independently recomputed by brute force over all 105 host pairs and matched exactly, and the full analysis is byte-for-byte deterministic across runs under the frozen seeds 36287179392 (bootstrap), 36287179393 (nulls) and 36287179394 (positive control).

AGF is unbounded above by construction, because one signature can match on every host pair. The value 83.51 is therefore not a fraction in [0,1] despite prereg 7.3 calling it a fraction, and cannot be compared to any externally reported prevalence number without that accounting convention.
unresolved: The frozen question is unanswered and stays unanswered: what fraction of observed navigational and interaction structure is alias-generalizable across distinct eTLD+1 hosts, relative to a null of demonstrated power. The frozen null is an identity, so the packet cannot answer it, and no answer is claimed here.

Whether real cross-site alias-generalizable structure exists at all in a form SPIDER could inherit remains open. The powered supplementary analysis places the measured sharing at or below a random re-partition of the same vocabulary, which is evidence against the specific mechanism the frozen statistic can see, but it is not a bounded negative on C-CROSSSITE, because the frozen statistic cannot distinguish reusable task structure from shared boilerplate.

The measured cost floor is a floor for HTTP-observable structure only. The corresponding floor for a client-rendered site is NOT_MEASURED, with the exact blocking artefact being the absence of any browser binary and the absence of same-origin anchors in the raw HTML of crates.io. The smallest unblocking action is a credential-free credentialed-free rendering substrate, or an explicit decision to bound the product thesis to static-HTML sites.

Whether the 4 unmeasured-but-reachable hosts (crates.io, kernel.org) and the 3 User-Agent-blocked hosts (npmjs.com, sourceforge.net, stackoverflow.com) would change the prevalence result is unknown. The frozen prereg forbids adaptive sampling, so this was not probed with alternative User-Agents or renderers.

The direction of the powered-null result needs an independent check before any lane re-scopes on it. The supplementary null NC-SIG-REASSIGN was constructed by the producer, not by the frozen design, and its choice of preserving per-host counts and the global multiset is one defensible randomisation among several. AUDIT should confirm or dispute that construction before the finding is used to deprioritise a claim.

No external baseline number is produced by this packet, so the director_mandate question about setting SPIDER's external baseline set by measurement rather than by reported numbers is addressed only for the observation-cost side, where 3 internal baselines (raw HTML, full DOM, accessibility approximation) were measured on the same 155 observations. The cross-site prevalence side produced no usable bar.
